tier_reason: Tier upgraded from D to C. The repo has no numbers, but a rust-lang/rust issue comment by rustc-hash maintainer N. Nethercote gives first-party rustc-perf results: switching rustc from FxHasher back to std DefaultHasher (SipHash-1-3) regressed every `check` benchmark by 3.9%-84.7%. Hardware, compiler flags and metric are not stated, and the measurement is of the pre-2.0 algorithm, so it cannot go above C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Switching rustc's FxHashMap/FxHashSet from FxHasher back to std's DefaultHasher (SipHash-1-3, with the #69152 improvements) regressed every rustc-perf `check` benchmark by 3.9% to 84.7%. Examples: deeply-nested-check avg 63.6% (max 84.7%), syn-check avg 38.7%, helloworld-check avg 23.3%, token-stream-stress-check avg 5.9%. Measured locally in Feb 2020 on the pre-2.0 Firefox-derived FxHash. The Rust Performance Book summarizes this as 'slowdowns ranging from 4-84%'.
corrections.baseline: SipHash-1-3 (Rust std DefaultHasher, the default hasher of std::collections::HashMap/HashSet)
corrections.workload: Hashing inside rustc's internal hash maps/sets (integers, composite multi-integer keys, short strings/slices), measured as end-to-end rustc compile time on rustc-perf `check` benchmarks
corrections.stars_or_usage: 597 stars; ~828M all-time crates.io downloads (~225M recent); internal hasher (FxHashMap/FxHashSet) throughout the rustc compiler
corrections.caveats: The numbers are first-party end-to-end rustc-perf compile-time results that a rustc/rustc-hash maintainer measured locally in Feb 2020. Hardware, compiler flags and the exact metric are not stated. They cover the old Firefox-derived FxHash. The current 2.x hasher (Orson Peters' polynomial hash with rotation finalizer and wyhash-style string compression) is described only as 'slightly better performance for rustc' in the CHANGELOG, and 2.0 caused a large-hashmap regression in rustc that 2.1.1 mitigated. In the same comment, std HashMap was slightly faster than FxHashMap on an integer-key microbenchmark (fewer collisions). FxHash is not HashDoS-resistant. The repo has no benchmark code (benchmarks PR #50 was closed unmerged).

notes: The repo README has no numbers. The real numbers page is the rust-lang/rust #69153 comment, which the Rust Performance Book hashing chapter cites. GitHub detects only Apache-2.0, but Cargo.toml says 'Apache-2.0 OR MIT' and both LICENSE files are present, so the license is corrected. last_commit 2026-07-18, active status, the 597 stars and the 827M+ downloads were all checked and are correct.
